decision: CI runs the offline check suite on every PR and blocks a script failure; a non-reproducing rebuild or a FAIL not in qa/known_fails.csv

decision: Raw documents (L0) kept as sha256-named assets of the private repo's l0-archive release; index meta/l0_archive.csv; a file without a recorded sha256 is accepted only when its cited amounts are on its cited pages
why: 13 GB and files over 100 MB do not fit git history; release assets keep clones light

decision: Licence: every series records licence and redistribution (never guessed); to_confirm does not block publishing official figures with full citation and the publisher named (owner decision 2026-11-04); no_redistribution never leaves the warehouse; a takedown request is honoured
why: legal exposure

decision: Personal data: individuals are natural_person entities held only for a recorded public-interest purpose and never returned by tools or views; names masked in output
why: PDPA

decision: Defamation: a named body is linked to a finding or contract in public only by a code_exact or human_signed link
why: one wrong match is a defamation exposure

decision: Neutrality: methods declared before results are seen; every view covers all 13 states and 3 Federal Territories; no party attribute in the core; elections only as geographic context
why: credibility across the political spectrum

decision: Lawful sources only: published by the owner; released under law; or obtained through an official data request; no leaked or OSA-classified documents
why: legal exposure

decision: Conflicts of interest: where IKRAM or its people helped produce a source a caveat discloses it on every answer that uses it
why: transparency

decision: Sensitive breakdowns: ethnicity published only as the official source publishes it; never inferred
why: legal and social sensitivity

decision: A source document whose PDF cannot be archived (publisher link dead, no other official copy found) keeps its extracted figures, marked 'PDF not archived' on every answer that uses them; first case PKKP FY2020 (ANM returns 404)
why: the figures were extracted and checked against the volume's own totals before the link died; dropping them would lose audited data, hiding the gap would overstate verifiability

decision: Where the publisher's own copy is gone, a public mirror of an official document (e.g. Sinar Project govdocs) may be archived, but only when it passes the identity check (our cited amounts on our cited pages, meta/l0_identity.py); its source_url in meta/l0_archive.csv shows it is a mirror, and its sha256 is its own (a re-saved copy is not byte-identical to the original)
why: keeps the archive verifiable without trusting the mirror: the check proves it is the same published volume

decision: Entity identity (Phase 3): a federal body is its supply vote. A B code keeps one entity_id through renames and portfolio changes while it is printed every year; its P code belongs to the same body, including the years after the B vote ends (the residual development vote). A B vote printed again after a lapse is a NEW entity unless a person links it (decision_status=proposed until then). Renumberings link only with a proof (B.41->B.63 and B.49->B.64, approved before the register). Tanggungan (T.*) and the contingency reserve (P.70) are spending heads, not bodies: entity = the federal government with a charged_head/reserve_head breakdown. entity_type gains 'department' and 'vote' (a vote administered by another body: B.11, B.12 under the Treasury). Budget books do not extend a lineage: they reprint lapsed votes with zeros.
why: readable codes are renumbered and reused (DATA_MODEL 4.5); a rule declared before the money is loaded keeps identity from being decided to fit a result; ID issuance stays a human decision
